actuation: antagonistic SCPAM strings (three bottom strings for forward bending, two top strings for backward recovery)
constitutive_assumptions: Variable stiffness sections of the finger are modeled as elastic cantilever beams under an applied vertical force at the fingertip.
The structural stiffness contributions of flexible polyimide heaters, aluminum foil tape, and soft actuators are neglected in the theoretical stiffness model due to their lightness and flexibility.
Bending deformation is assumed to occur exclusively at the three heated variable stiffness sections, while the connecting sections maintain constant high stiffness.
Small bending angle approximations are assumed (cos(theta_i) ≈ 1, cos(theta_1+theta_2) ≈ 1, cos(theta_1+theta_2+theta_3) ≈ 1, and sin(theta_i) ≈ theta_i).

The elastic modulus of SMP within its glass transition region (Tl < T < Th) is assumed to follow a logarithmic-linear relationship with temperature (Es = Eg * 10^(a * (Tg/T - 1))) and remains constant outside this region.
The temperature across the entire SMP thickness is approximated by the temperature measured on the backside of the SMP.
The finger force-displacement relationship is assumed to be approximately linear within the fingertip deflection range of 0 to 2 mm.
For kinematic trajectory modeling, each activated finger segment is assumed to produce an identical bending angle under 70 °C SMP temperature and identical input power per SCPAM string.
control_variables: Thermal imager measurement location and fixed distance
Fan distance (fan blade center fixed at 70 mm from SMP) and operating parameters (130 miniature DC motor, 12,000 rpm)
Target high temperature for activated SMP (Th = 70 °C / 343.15 K)
Electrical current per SCPAM string during bending tests (0.5 A)
Geometric parameters and material properties of the finger prototype (lengths L1 and L2, aluminum foil thickness 0.12 mm)
Displacement evaluation range for linear stiffness fitting (0 to 2 mm)
Sensor mounting position at the fingertip
dependent_variables: SMP and SCPAM temperature profiles over time during heating and cooling
Thermal radiation coupling and temperature fluctuations between SCPAM and SMP
Bending angle of the finger (overall angle and angle per activated segment)
Contact reaction force and finger stiffness k (slope of force-displacement response)
Initial force at 0 mm displacement resulting from actuator prestress release
Fingertip workspace trajectory under sequential and nonsequential motion modes
Grasping success, object retention, and load-bearing capacity
Contact surface area, contour conformability, and envelope range on target objects
Surface pressure distribution and indentation uniformity on deformable plasticine molds

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: The soft robotic finger achieves a maximum experimental stiffness ratio of 10.54 between room temperature (25 °C) and 70 °C with actuators on, and 25.91 with no actuators assembled.
Thermoplastic SMP undergoes a reversible transition between glass and rubber states over 40 °C to 70 °C, altering elastic modulus across three orders of magnitude from 2150 MPa to 2.1 MPa.

Laminating a 0.12 mm aluminum foil layer onto the SMP surface cuts the passive cooling time approximately in half (from ~160 s to ~80 s) and provides effective thermal radiation shielding between SCPAM actuators and SMP.

Applying 0.5 A per SCPAM string at 70 °C SMP temperature produces maximum bending angles of 23.21° for one segment, 41.24° (20.62°/segment) for two segments, and 48.27° (16.09°/segment) for three segments.
A theoretical cantilever beam model integrating a thermomechanical SMP constitutive relation predicts the experimental stiffness reduction trend as temperature rises from 25 °C to 70 °C.

Sequential activation of SMP segments from root to tip (1-2-3) expands the finger workspace, increases contact surface area, and distributes pressure more uniformly over curved objects than simultaneous nonsequential activation.
A two-finger soft gripper successfully grips and lifts a 150 g load when the SMP sections are cooled to a high-stiffness state, but drops the load if the heaters remain powered on.

experimental_setup: Thermal test bench: UNI-T UTi220A PRO thermal imager fixed in position, two KAIPUSEN K-type ultraminiature thermocouples adhered with UOWO YW7015 thermal conductive silicone, MAX6675 digitizer, PID temperature controller, and a 130-engine miniature cooling fan (1-6 V, 12,000 rpm) positioned 70 mm away.

Bending measurement platform: WitMotion JY61 six-axis motion processing unit (MPU6050, 1 g, 5 V, 0.05 A) affixed to the fingertip to track angular deflection during SCPAM actuation at 0.5 A per string.

Stiffness test platform: Stepper-motor-driven linear screw guide sliding from 0 to 5 mm in 0.5 mm increments, aluminum profile mounting frame, and an NSCING ES SH-III-20N digital force gauge contacting the fingertip.

Grasping evaluation setup: Two-finger soft robotic gripper mounted on a vertical linear screw guide to evaluate grasping on diverse objects (150 g solder wire roll, cylindrical popcorn box, roll of tape, triangular metal block, square object).

Conformability and pressure distribution apparatus: Cylindrical objects of varying diameters (aluminum tape d=122 mm, copper tape d=99 mm, insulation tape d=64 mm); custom cylindrical test piece fabricated from a 3-D printed resin mold with a 15 mm layer of plasticine at 120 mm diameter to capture contact indentations.
future_work: Developing closed-loop position control based on the existing thermocouple-monitored closed-loop temperature control system.
Optimizing the structural design and fabrication techniques of SCPAM actuators to increase contraction stroke and expand the bending angle of the soft finger.
Optimizing SMP and silicone rubber shell geometry (e.g., expanding through-hole area and count, or thinning SMP for low-load tasks) to accelerate passive cooling.
Investigating embedded fluid channels for active air or liquid cooling in speed-critical applications.
independent_variables: Actuator operational state (no actuators assembled, actuators configured but unpowered/off, actuators energized/on)
Electrical current supplied to PI electrothermal film heaters and SCPAM strings
Cooling mode (natural cooling without foil, natural cooling with aluminum foil tape, fan cooling)
Number and combination of selectively heated SMP segments (1, 2, or 3 segments; 8 bending configurations)
Segment activation sequence (root-to-tip sequential motion 1-2-3 versus nonsequential all-segment activation)
Applied fingertip displacement (0 to 5 mm via linear guide)
Geometry, diameter, and curvature of target grasping objects (cylindrical objects from 64 to 122 mm diameter, square, triangular)
limitations_inferred: The grasping demonstrations were restricted to lightweight objects (up to 150 g) and planar bending; torsional resistance, out-of-plane loading, and heavier payload capabilities were not characterized.

Long-term cycling durability, fatigue life, and interfacial bonding integrity between the silicone shell, SMP, PI heaters, and adhesive under cyclic thermal and mechanical stresses were not evaluated.
Prestress inherent to the assembled SCPAM strings induces uncommanded initial tip deformation and force when the SMP softens, even before actuators are electrically energized.
Even with passive cooling enhancements (reducing cooling time to ~80 s), the thermal cycle duration remains relatively long for high-speed or dynamic manipulation tasks.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Natural air cooling of the SMP sections within the silicone shell is slow, taking roughly 160 s without foil to drop from 70 °C to 40 °C.
SCPAM actuators exhibit limited actuation bandwidth (0.3 Hz in still air, 1 Hz in forced air) and low energy efficiency (0.71% to 1.32%).
Thermal coupling between the Joule-heated SMP and SCPAM actuators is inevitable during thermal operation and can alter stiffness or actuation states if unshielded.
Heater current must be constrained to avoid thermal damage to the flexible PI electrothermal films.

Fan cooling introduces rigid motor components that compromise soft robot compliance, whereas active liquid or pneumatic cooling requires redundant and bulky auxiliary hardware outside the paper's scope.

Theoretical beam modeling omits the stiffness of heaters, aluminum foil, wiring, actuators, and probe contact compliance, causing overprediction of stiffness at low temperatures and underprediction at high temperatures.
Precise closed-loop position control was not implemented; only closed-loop temperature control was achieved.
The contraction property of current SCPAM actuators limits the achievable bending angle of the finger.
main_results: Successfully integrated shape memory polymers (SMP) for segmental stiffness modulation and supercoiled polymer artificial muscles (SCPAM) for bending actuation into a compact, fully electrically/thermally activated soft robotic finger.
Incorporating a 0.12 mm aluminum foil layer halved the SMP passive cooling time from ~160 s to ~80 s and effectively suppressed thermal radiation cross-talk between the actuators and SMP.

Finger bending angle scaled with the number of activated segments (23.21° for one segment, 41.24° for two, and 48.27° for three under 0.5 A/string at 70 °C), while the deflection per individual section decreased.
Experimental finger stiffness dropped monotonically with temperature, demonstrating a variable stiffness ratio of 25.91 without actuators and 10.54 with actuators powered on between 25 °C and 70 °C.
A closed-form beam bending model incorporating Tobushi's thermomechanical constitutive equation captured the measured stiffness trends across the 25 °C to 70 °C range.

A two-finger gripper demonstrated successful grasping and lifting of a 150 g object at high stiffness (cooled state), whereas the object was dropped when attempted in the low-stiffness (heated) state.

Root-to-tip sequential activation (1-2-3) produced an expanded workspace envelope, larger object contact area, and more uniform pressure distribution on curved surfaces compared to nonsequential activation.
modeling_methods: Cantilever beam bending formulation relating fingertip vertical force to tip displacement (k = F / delta).
Segmental deflection modeling summing the vertical displacement contributions across the three variable-stiffness SMP sections and four constant-stiffness connecting sections.
Beam moment and curvature equations (theta_i = M_i * L_1 / (E_SV * I_S + E_R * I_R)).
Small-deflection approximations (cos(theta) ≈ 1, sin(theta) ≈ theta) to derive an analytical expression for overall finger stiffness k.
Tobushi thermomechanical constitutive relation modeling SMP elastic modulus as a function of temperature across the glass transition zone.
Linear regression fitting on experimental force-displacement data within the 0 to 2 mm range to determine stiffness.
Kinematic tip trajectory analysis comparing sequential and nonsequential motion configurations.
performance_metrics: Variable stiffness ratio: 10.54 (actuators on) and 25.91 (no actuators) between 25 °C and 70 °C
SMP elastic modulus range: 2150 MPa (El at 40 °C) to 2.1 MPa (Eh at 70 °C), with Eg = 57.35 MPa at Tg = 55 °C (three orders of magnitude variation)
Cooling duration from 70 °C to 40 °C: ~160 s (natural cooling without foil), ~80 s (natural cooling with aluminum foil), ~50 s (cooling from Tg to Tl with foil), and ~35 s (fan cooling)
Maximum bending angles (at 70 °C, 0.5 A/string): 23.21° (1 section), 41.24° (2 sections, 20.62°/section), and 48.27° (3 sections, 16.09°/segment)
Maximum load-bearing in grasping demonstration: successfully lifted 150 g solder wire roll
Actuation bandwidth and efficiency benchmarks for SCPAM: 0.3 Hz in standing air / 1 Hz in forced air, power efficiency 0.71% to 1.32%, and power density 27 W/g
possible_gap_implications: Combining Joule-heated SMPs and SCPAMs provides an all-electric, compressor-free architecture for variable-stiffness soft grippers, indicating a viable design direction for compact, untethered soft manipulators if thermal cooling latency and actuation bandwidth constraints can be alleviated.

Segment-by-segment stiffness control enabling sequential conformability highlights how localized compliance tuning can substitute for complex multi-actuator kinematic controls in soft grasping, although achieving high-speed grasping cycles requires rapid active thermal management.
paper.research_objective: To design, model, fabricate, and experimentally characterize a compact soft robotic finger capable of both segmental variable stiffness and tunable bending shape by integrating thermoresponsive shape memory polymers (SMPs) with polyimide flexible film heaters for stiffness modulation and supercoiled polymer artificial muscles (SCPAMs) for actuation.
paper.research_problem: Soft robots typically exhibit low structural stiffness, limiting their force output and load-bearing capacity, while conventional stiffness modulation mechanisms (such as jamming, SMAs, MRFs/ERFs, LMPAs, or external fluidic lines) often introduce bulk, high stiffness in flexible states, slow switching, or unsafe driving voltages; additionally, conventional soft fingers lack flexible shape adaptability and sequential motion to conform stably to diverse object geometries.
paper.robot_type: soft robotic finger (configured into a soft robotic gripper)
stiffness_mechanism: thermoplastic SMP with glass-to-rubber phase transition
flexible polyimide (PI) electrothermal film heaters for segmental Joule heating
paper.title: A Novel Variable Stiffness and Tunable Bending Shape Soft Robotic Finger Based on Thermoresponsive Polymers
